domain: team dinner at an Ethiopian restaurant
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant recommendation and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a group dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a Friday dinner at an Ethiopian restaurant for office colleagues. You will introduce 5 people with various dietary needs in a burst, then updates will come: one person drops out, one person's allergy gets corrected, and a new person joins. At the end you will share a specific menu and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be — you genuinely want the assistant to check.

You are a calm, cooperative office organizer. You always refer to your colleagues by name in third person (e.g. 'Marcus told me...', 'Priya mentioned...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal coordination among friends.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for colleague updates

ground_truth.answer: Kitfo (raw minced beef) is problematic for Nina — she is 7 months pregnant and cannot eat raw meat. Doro Wat (chicken stew) and Tibs (sautéed beef) are problematic for Priya — she is Jain and cannot eat meat. Gomen (collard greens sautéed with garlic) is problematic for Priya — strict Jain practice forbids root vegetables including garlic. Misir Wat (spiced red lentils) is fine for everyone. Injera (teff flatbread) is fine for everyone including Marcus — teff is naturally gluten-free. Spicy dishes are no longer a concern since Derek dropped out.
required_elements: Kitfo is problematic for Nina because it is raw beef and she is 7 months pregnant (no raw meat during pregnancy)
Doro Wat is problematic for Priya because it contains chicken (meat) and she is Jain
Tibs is problematic for Priya because it contains beef (meat) and she is Jain
Gomen is problematic for Priya because it is sautéed with garlic, and strict Jain practice forbids root vegetables including garlic
Injera is safe for Marcus — teff is gluten-free, so his celiac disease is not triggered
Misir Wat (spiced red lentils) is fine for everyone currently attending
forbidden_elements: Flagging injera as problematic for Marcus (teff is gluten-free, not wheat-based)
Flagging spicy dishes as a problem (Derek who doesn't like spicy food already dropped out)
Flagging sesame-containing items for Tomoko (her allergy was corrected to tree nuts, sesame is fine)
Saying Tomoko has a sesame allergy (it was retested and corrected to tree nut allergy)
Ignoring Gomen's garlic as a problem for Priya (garlic is a root vegetable forbidden in strict Jain diet)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning. Key challenges: (1) Injera is the HIDDEN INGREDIENT TRAP — it looks like bread/flatbread which would trigger celiac concerns, but injera is made from teff flour which is naturally gluten-free, so Marcus is fine. Models that over-generalize 'flatbread = gluten' will incorrectly flag it. (2) Gomen contains garlic (a root vegetable) which violates Priya's strict Jain diet — this is a hidden ingredient issue since 'collard greens' sounds safe but the garlic preparation makes it problematic. (3) Kitfo is raw beef — Nina is 7 months pregnant (late-joining entity) so raw meat is unsafe. (4) Derek's spicy preference was REMOVED when he dropped out. (5) Tomoko's sesame allergy was CORRECTED to tree nut — the agent must not flag sesame-containing items. The scenario has 3 lifecycle events: Derek exits (constraint removal), Tomoko's allergy corrected (constraint upgrade/change), Nina joins late (new constraint).

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
